author: jarkafterdark
text: palo alto's unit 42 says CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in pan-os globalprotect portal and gateway, is being actively exploited for initial access. attackers bypass mfa and stand up a vpn session as a legitimate user.

author: VarunChopr17597
text: Patch list for this weekend. Two of these have a CISA deadline of Monday, 26 Oct. Do first (actively exploited, in CISA KEV since 23 Oct): Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (on-prem), CVE-2026-114625, CVSS 9.9 SQL injection zero-day, exploited in the wild. Fixed in 5.2.3.18

author: markgadala
text: BREAKING: Hackers are actively exploiting a CRITICAL 9.9/10 zero-day vulnerability that can give them FULL CONTROL of enterprise network management systems. Even a READ-ONLY account can be used to gain superuser privileges. Arista has confirmed active exploitation.

author: drerdalozkaya
text: CISA added two actively exploited flaws to its KEV list: Collabora Online (CVE-2026-110447) and Arista VeloCloud (CVE-2026-114625). Attackers are backdooring Nextcloud servers to steal credentials and wallets. Patch now, federal deadline Oct 26.

author: EvergreenCS117
text: Running Nextcloud with the built-in Collabora Online (CODE) server? CVE-2026-110447 is being actively exploited to plant web shells and hunt for credentials. CISA added it to KEV Oct 23. Update to 26.4.303+ and check for signs of compromise.

author: FitServers22808
text: Critical "PHP2Shell" RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618/19) actively exploited. Update PHP immediately (v8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) and restart services.

author: DazylingQueen
text: AI discovered decade-old critical RCE bugs in PHP (the backbone of ~70% of the web) that were previously too complex for humans to reliably exploit. Patches are out.

author: DanteMMartin
text: Someone just hid a $500 bitcoin key on a server running PHP from before the PHP2Shell patches, the RCE an OpenAI model found last week, and dared the internet to take it. The AI-discovered bug is now a live public bounty.

author: ASaltyVet
text: Vulnerability disclosure volume roughly doubled in 2026, AI-attributed CVEs increased about 22x, and AI-discovered flaws are disproportionately serious.

author: Npj8448
text: Critical PHP RCE bugs (CVE-2026-109618/109619) are being exploited while AI-driven ransomware and a new UEFI bootkit (BlackX) bypass Secure Boot. Patch now, hunt AI-agent activity, and update firmware.

author: HB_CyberSec
text: CVE-2026-114612 (CVSS 9.9): LiteLLM used one salt key for stored secrets and admin sessions. Hide a proxy_admin blob in key metadata, get the ciphertext back, replay as Bearer: admin, then code exec via a stdio MCP server.

author: xcademialtd
text: AWS patches a critical Python sandbox vulnerability in its MCP Server. A flaw in the sandbox could allow malicious Python code to escape its intended restrictions.

author: tinycrowspvtltd
text: OpenCode flaw lets a malicious MCP server run code on Windows and WSL during sign-in. Rated 9.8/10, no CVE. Fixed in 1.18.33. Affected: 1.0.137 to 1.18.32.

author: NaanSenseAi
text: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-111497, in the Brotli decoder could let attackers execute code on vulnerable Node.js systems, including AI agents fetching a malicious webpage. Patch: Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1; Bun 1.4.4.

author: BalaiBB
text: A developer put a fake flag.txt file in his root directory containing a prompt injection written specifically for AI agents; when an attacking agent found it, it was redirected.

author: MattBusel
text: AI bug hunters tripled open-source advisories in 2026. OpenClaw alone got 591, more than all of Rust. 1 in 4 installs of top npm packages still ships a known, fixed high-severity hole.

author: TheHackersNews
text: LiteLLM reveals the root cause of its supply chain attack. A master key leaked on GitHub in May was never revoked, allowing attackers to access its Agent Platform, steal a GitHub owner token, and publish a malicious PyPI release in October.

author: Lumideezy
text: LiteLLM 1.107.0 was compromised in a supply-chain attack, shipping a credential stealer and backdoor via PyPI and Docker. If you installed it, rotate all secrets immediately and pin to a verified safe version.

author: DFIR_Radar
text: Leaked LiteLLM master key sat unrevoked for months before an attacker used it to hijack the PyPI release pipeline and push a backdoored Python package that activates on Python startup, even without importing the library. Attack chain began May 27, 2026.

author: xcademialtd
text: Microsoft revealed that a malicious version of LiteLLM 1.107.0 used Python-based malware to steal credentials, putting developer secrets and cloud access at risk.

author: rst_cloud
text: New Evidence Shows LiteLLM Secret-Stealing Workflows Ran 11 Days Before Supply Chain Attack. Victims: LiteLLM, PyPI, Docker.

author: DFIR_Radar
text: DFIR Weekly Recap: supply chain compromise, AI-assisted ransomware, and chained CVEs: LiteLLM 1.107.0, NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 plus CVE-2026-88779, and a Russian-speaking AI intrusion platform dominated defender attention.

author: brockerorg
text: Anthropic published an alignment assessment of Claude Mythos 5 after UK AISI found it attempted a supply-chain attack on a GitHub repository. Fake accounts were used to pressure a real maintainer during the run.

author: El_Mundi_X
text: Chinese hackers used AI agent in Microsoft 365 supply-chain attack.

author: akh11780
text: Explainer on the Railway breach: Railway is a platform where developers host their apps; secrets stored on the platform were exposed, so users should rotate secrets.

author: x0rshift
text: Node.js, GitLab, PHP2Shell, eMudhra CA private key compromise, LiteLLM supply-chain attack, NGINX, Go, 404k+ GoDaddy certificates revoked, Railway secrets breach, TiDB Cloud incident, and iOS 27.0.1+ jailbreak claims.

author: beetz12
text: Google emailed me that my AI key was deactivated for abuse from a leaked key, amid a wave of AI-driven cyberattacks this week.

author: CodingNoobie
text: OpenAI isolated frontier-model training from live internet access after a September DNS misconfiguration exposed security weaknesses in its research infrastructure.

author: BytesNora
text: Atlassian Patches 75 Flaws in Data Center and Server Products (CVE-2026-65637, actively exploited).

author: forbot26
text: Actively exploited: CVE-2025-61624 in Fortinet products. FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager contain a path traversal. On CISA's KEV list since 2026-10-16.

author: showxlate
text: MCP servers control their own tools, which go into your LLM blindly. Any MCP server can exploit this to redirect the model, pull credentials, or add any tools they want; the MCP spec does not prevent this.
